target: Volevo che tu venissi alla mia festa.
english: I wanted you to come to my party.
tip: "Venissi" – imperfect subjunctive of venire, after past tense main clause.

target: Ero appena arrivato quando è iniziato a piovere.
english: I had just arrived when it started raining.
tip: Trapassato prossimo with essere: ero arrivato.

target: Se avessi studiato di più da giovane, ora sarei preparato.
english: If I had studied more when young, I'd now be prepared.
tip: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result.

target: Se parlassi italiano perfettamente, vivrei a Roma.
english: If I spoke Italian perfectly, I'd live in Rome.
tip: Regular -are verbs: parlassi, parlassi, parlasse, parlassimo, parlaste, parlassero.

target: Se dovesse piovere, la partita viene rinviata.
english: If it should rain, the game will be postponed.
tip: Passive voice: essere/venire + past participle. "Il libro è stato scritto" (The book was written).

target: Se arrivi prima, prendimi un caffè al bar.
english: If you arrive first, get me a coffee at the bar.
tip: Type 3 (past unreal): 'Se avessi studiato, avrei passato' = If I had studied, I would have passed.

target: Bisogna fare attenzione.
english: One must pay attention.
tip: 'Bisogna' + infinitive for impersonal necessity.

target: Penso che lui abbia ragione.
english: I think he's right.
tip: The subjunctive is triggered by 'penso che' (I think that).

target: Bisogna che tu parta subito.
english: You need to leave right away.
tip: Bisogna che requires the subjunctive.

target: Prima che tu parta, salutami.
english: Before you leave, say goodbye to me.
tip: 'Prima che' always requires the subjunctive.

target: Credo che sia una buona idea.
english: I think it's a good idea.
tip: Sia is the subjunctive of essere, triggered by 'credo che'.

target: Voglio che tu venga alla festa.
english: I want you to come to the party.
tip: Volere che + subjunctive expresses a wish for someone else's action.

target: Venne a sapere la verità troppo tardi.
english: He found out the truth too late.
tip: 'Venire a' + infinitive: achievement.

target: La porta viene chiusa alle sei di sera.
english: The door is closed at six in the evening.
tip: Passive with venire: emphasizes the action happening regularly.

target: Stavo dormendo quando il telefono ha cominciato a squillare.
english: I was sleeping when the phone started ringing.
tip: "Stare" + gerund forms the progressive aspect in Italian.

target: La pizza è mangiata da tutti.
english: Pizza is eaten by everyone.
tip: Passive voice: essere + past participle + da.

target: In Italia si mangia bene.
english: In Italy people eat well.
tip: 'Si' impersonal: si + third person for general statements.

target: Qui si vendono prodotti locali.
english: Local products are sold here.
tip: "Si" passivante with plural: verb agrees with the noun. "Si vendono case" = Houses are sold. The noun is the grammatical subject.

target: Se fossi te, lo farei senza pensarci.
english: If I were you, I'd do it without thinking.
tip: "Se fossi te" – common Type 2 structure for giving advice.

target: Poiché era tardi, abbiamo deciso di prendere un taxi.
english: Since it was late, we decided to take a taxi.
tip: "Poiché" – formal connector meaning 'since/because', usually at sentence start.

target: Ha spiegato che aveva perso il treno per un solo minuto.
english: He explained that he had missed the train by just one minute.
tip: In indirect speech, passato prossimo shifts to trapassato prossimo.

target: Se piove, resto a casa.
english: If it rains, I stay home.
tip: Periodo ipotetico della realtà: se + presente, presente.

target: La cena verrà servita alle otto.
english: Dinner will be served at eight.
tip: Passive with venire for ongoing/habitual actions.

target: Si vendono appartamenti in centro città.
english: Apartments are for sale in the city center.
tip: Si passivante: si + verb (3rd person) – impersonal passive construction.

target: Quando si è stanchi, tutto sembra più difficile.
english: When one is tired, everything seems harder.
tip: "Si è" – impersonal with essere, adjective agrees in plural.

target: Il libro è stato scritto da un autore famoso.
english: The book was written by a famous author.
tip: 'Si' makes impersonal statements: 'Si mangia bene qui' = One eats well here / The food is good here.

target: Se lei fosse venuta con noi, si sarebbe divertita.
english: If she had come with us, she would have had fun.
tip: "Si" impersonal/passive: "Si mangia bene qui" (One eats well here / You eat well here). Very common in Italian.

target: Pur sapendo la verità, ha deciso di non dire niente.
english: Despite knowing the truth, he decided not to say anything.
tip: "Pur" + gerund – concessive: 'despite/although doing'.

target: Comincia a fare freddo.
english: It's starting to get cold.
tip: 'Cominciare a' + infinitive: beginning.

target: Non credo che mia sorella sappia ancora la notizia.
english: I don't believe my sister knows the news yet.
tip: "Sappia" is the subjunctive of "sapere" (to know).

target: Bisogna che tu faccia attenzione a ogni piccolo dettaglio.
english: You need to pay attention to every small detail.
tip: "Bisogna che" (it is necessary that) triggers subjunctive.

target: Non riesco a dormire quando fa troppo caldo la notte.
english: I can't sleep when it's too hot at night.
tip: "Riuscire a" + infinitive means to manage/succeed in doing something.

target: Per quanto ne sappia, nessuno ha ancora trovato una soluzione.
english: As far as I know, nobody has found a solution yet.
tip: "Per quanto" (as far as / however much) triggers subjunctive.

target: Il progetto è da rifare.
english: The project needs redoing.
tip: 'Essere da' + infinitive: necessity.

target: La pizza è fatta in Italia da secoli.
english: Pizza has been made in Italy for centuries.
tip: Passive with essere: subject + essere + past participle (+ da agent).

target: Nonostante la pioggia, la festa è stata un successo.
english: Despite the rain, the party was a success.
tip: "Nonostante" + noun – 'despite'.

target: Ho da fare tutto il pomeriggio; ci vediamo stasera.
english: I have things to do all afternoon – see you tonight.
tip: "Avere da" + infinitive expresses obligation or things to be done.

target: Questa storia va raccontata per non dimenticare il passato.
english: This story must be told so as not to forget the past.
tip: "Andare" + past participle expresses obligation (must be done).

target: A meno che non cambi idea, parto domani mattina presto.
english: Unless I change my mind, I'm leaving early tomorrow morning.
tip: "A meno che non" (unless) requires subjunctive; the "non" is pleonastic.

target: Cerco un hotel che abbia una vista panoramica sul mare.
english: I'm looking for a hotel that has a panoramic sea view.
tip: Subjunctive in relative clauses when the antecedent is indefinite or sought.

target: Senza che nessuno se ne accorga, è uscita di nascosto ieri.
english: Without anyone noticing, she snuck out yesterday.
tip: "Senza che" (without) requires the subjunctive.

target: Ha smesso di fumare due anni fa per motivi di salute.
english: He quit smoking two years ago for health reasons.
tip: "Smettere di" + infinitive means to stop/quit doing something.

target: Si stava meglio quando si stava peggio.
english: Things were better when they were worse.
tip: "Si" impersonal: "Si dice che..." = People say that... "Si" + 3rd person verb for general statements without a specific subject.

target: Tuttavia, non sono d'accordo.
english: However, I don't agree.
tip: 'Tuttavia' is a formal connector meaning 'however'.

target: Anzi, penso il contrario.
english: On the contrary, I think the opposite.
tip: 'Anzi' corrects or strengthens a previous statement.

target: Ha finito di lavorare tardi.
english: He finished working late.
tip: 'Finire di' + infinitive: completion.

target: Malgrado le difficoltà, ce l'ha fatta.
english: Despite the difficulties, he made it.
tip: 'Malgrado' is a formal synonym of 'nonostante'.

target: Gli ho detto di non preoccuparsi.
english: I told him not to worry.
tip: Imperative becomes 'di + infinitive' in reported speech.

target: Ha risposto che non sapeva nulla.
english: He replied that he didn't know anything.
tip: 'Chiedere se' (to ask whether) introduces indirect questions: 'Mi ha chiesto se volevo venire'.

target: Continua a piovere da tre giorni senza interruzione.
english: It has been raining for three days without interruption.
tip: "Continuare a" + infinitive expresses ongoing, persistent action.

target: Ha detto che era stanco e che voleva riposarsi.
english: He said he was tired and that he wanted to rest.
tip: In reported speech, present tense becomes imperfect: "sono stanco" → "era stanco".

target: Il treno sta per partire; dobbiamo correre al binario.
english: The train is about to leave – we have to run to the platform.
tip: "Stare per" signals something is on the verge of happening.

target: Mi sono abituato a svegliarmi presto per andare a correre.
english: I got used to waking up early to go running.
tip: "Abituarsi a" + infinitive = to get used to doing something.

target: Mia madre ha detto che stava bene e non preoccuparsi.
english: My mother said she was fine and told me not to worry.
tip: Present → imperfect in reported speech; imperative → infinitive.

target: Scusa, sai dove si trova la stazione centrale qui vicino?
english: Sorry, do you know where the central station is near here?
tip: "Scusa" (tu) vs "Mi scusi" (Lei) marks the formality register shift.

target: Saranno le tre del pomeriggio; il sole è ancora alto.
english: It must be about three in the afternoon – the sun is still high.
tip: Simple future of probability: "saranno" = they must be (conjecture).

target: Continuano a lamentarsi senza motivo.
english: They keep complaining for no reason.
tip: 'Continuare a' + infinitive: ongoing action.

target: Quindi, è inutile continuare a discutere.
english: So, it's pointless to keep arguing.
tip: Verb + a/di + infinitive: continuare a (continue to), smettere di (stop), cominciare a (begin to). The preposition is fixed.

target: Ha smesso di fumare un anno fa.
english: He stopped smoking a year ago.
tip: 'Smettere di' + infinitive: cessation.

target: Mi sono fatto aiutare da un esperto.
english: I got help from an expert.
tip: 'Farsi' + infinitive: having something done for oneself.
